subject: Cross-border processor routing and controls — mitigation proposal
messages:
From: Nadia Albright <nadia.albright@veridianhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Processor routing & controls - initial TIA questions

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for the intro call earlier. Attached is Veridian's filled TIA questionnaire — our Vendor Risk team flagged a few items we need clarified around processor routing, chaining, and evidence for contractual flow-down. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood guarantee regional routing (EU-only) for certain datasets and provide proof in the form of logs or routing policy?
- Do you have an upstream contractual requirement for your subprocessors (i.e., flow-down)?
- If you use a subprocessor chain (sub-subprocessors), how is that disclosed and how quickly can you produce evidence?

We also need an updated subprocessor inventory (including region, function, and where they store/process EU data) and your current DPA redline. I attached our Vendor_Risk_Form.xlsx in case that's easier for your risk/compliance team to fill.

Happy to schedule a short follow-up next week — we want to keep the timeline tight.

Attachments: TIA_questionnaire_filled.pdf, Vendor_Risk_Form.xlsx

Best,
Nadia Albright
Head of Vendor Risk — Veridian Health
nadia.albright@veridianhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Albright <nadia.albright@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processor routing & controls - initial TIA questions

Nadia — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned to move fast. I've attached: our current DPA redline (DPA_redline_v3.docx) and the latest subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_Q3.csv). High-level replies below; follow-ups and legal language proposals are in a separate note.

Key points (summary):
- Regional routing: we support route-by-region policies at the request of the customer. For EU-tagged datasets we can pin requests to EU-hosted capacity (EU region routing) and provide request routing logs for the retention window you need — we typically retain routing traces for 90 days but can discuss extended retention under contract.
- Flow-down: Redwood requires subprocessors to accept flow-down clauses in the DPA. We maintain written flow-down obligations covering data handling, breach notification, and audit rights.
- Subprocessor chaining: we do allow sub-subprocessors in limited cases (e.g., managed storage tiers) but we require contractual flow-down and pre-notification (default 30 days). We can discuss shortening notification windows when justified.

Proposed mitigations for Veridian:
1) Add an SLA-backed routing commitment for EU-tagged traffic plus weekly routing logs (CSV export).
2) Include a 30-day pre-notice for new subprocessors + obligation to provide on-demand evidence within 7 business days.
3) Offer an optional UK IDTA / UK Addendum acceptance for UK personal data and map that to our TIA artifacts (SCC matrix + technical mappings).

Next steps:
- Karthik will propose precise clause text for the DPA and the UK IDTA addendum.
- Monica will update the subprocessor inventory to include storage region and primary contact.
- We can schedule a 30-min sync to walk through any redlines — propose Thu 10/07 10:00 AM BST / 02:00 AM PDT (please advise).

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx, subprocessor_inventory_Q3.csv

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Tom Murphy <tom.murphy@veridianhealth.com>

Date: 2027-10-01T08:27:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Processor routing & controls - initial TIA questions

Marissa — appreciate the quick turn. A couple of clarifying asks from our side after reviewing your redline and inventory: 

- On routing logs: can you commit to a signed representation that routing records show EU-only egress for the pinned capacity? Our team insists on an auditable chain (IP ranges + datacenter region).
- On subprocessor notice: 30 days is ok but the decision team prefers 14 days for critical subprocessors — can Redwood accept a 14-day notice window for ‘security-critical’ subprocessors?
- On UK IDTA: we need confirmation that if UK Addendum is executed, Redwood will treat UK data under IDTA terms and provide the UK evidence pack (mapping to SCC clauses).

I attached our Vendor_Risk_Form.xlsx with a couple of fields left blank — if your legal/compliance team can populate those it will speed the risk review. Also attaching a short export-control question set.

Attachments: Vendor_Risk_Form.xlsx, export_controls_brief.pdf

Thanks — Tom
Tom Murphy
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager — Veridian Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: DPA clause proposals & UK IDTA mapping

Team — tagging this thread with draft legal guidance based on Veridian's asks. Summary of what we can offer and proposed language snippets are attached (DPA_clause_snippets.txt). Top-level: SCCs + UK IDTA, explicit flow-down, enhanced notice windows for critical subprocessors, and evidence delivery SLA.

Proposed items (high-level):
- Routing representation (contractual): "Redwood represents that where Customer configures region-bound processing for EU jurisdiction, Redwood will implement routing controls such that egress from EU-located physical infrastructure will be used for processing and storage. Redwood will provide routing logs (IP range, datacenter, timestamp) upon request within the evidence SLA period."

- Subprocessor notice & evidence: "Redwood will provide prior notice of new subprocessors via the dashboard and in writing. For subprocessors classified as 'security-critical' by Customer, Redwood will use reasonable efforts to provide 14 days' notice; for all others, 30 days. Redwood will supply contractual flow-down and, upon Customer request, evidence of flow-down within 7 business days."

- UK IDTA / Addendum: "Upon execution of the UK IDTA addendum, Redwood will map the UK Addendum obligations to the corresponding SCC clauses and include a UK evidence package (transfer impact assessment, technical and organizational measures, and subprocessor mapping) within 10 business days of request."

Operational asks for Marissa/Monica:
- Monica: augment the inventory with primary contact + storage region column and mark subprocessors that are 'security-critical'.
- Marissa: agree on fallbacks (e.g., alternate EU-only model variant) and confirm whether we can extend routing logs retention for Veridian to 180 days under SOW.

Attaching: DPA_clause_snippets.txt (clause snippets), and I included a short checklist for the TIA pack.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cross-border processor routing and controls — mitigation proposal

Nadia / Tom — thanks for the detailed review and for the quick turn from your team. Quick summary / action items so we all have the same expectations: 

1) Routing commitment: Redwood will include a routing representation in the DPA and provide weekly routing logs (IP range, datacenter region, timestamp). We can extend retention to 180 days under an SOW.
2) Subprocessor notice: Redwood accepts 14-day notice for 'security-critical' subprocessors; 30 days otherwise. Evidence of flow-down will be provided within 7 business days upon request.
3) UK IDTA: Redwood will execute the UK Addendum for UK-personal-data scope and deliver a UK evidence pack (TIA mapping + TOMs) within 10 business days of request.

Next steps / timeline: 
- Karthik to insert the agreed snippets into the DPA redline and circulate (by 2027-10-08).
- Monica to publish the updated subprocessor inventory and tag security-critical entries (by 2027-10-07).
- Marissa to send proposed SOW language for extended log retention and routing SLA (by 2027-10-09).

Proposed follow-up call: 2027-10-12 09:00 AM BST. Please confirm availability and we'll send a calendar invite and DocuSign link for the updated DPA once legal has incorporated final language.

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.docx (updated in draft), subprocessor_inventory_Q3.csv, DPA_clause_snippets.txt

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.
